### 1. What the caller expresses, and simulator mode

- Target: "close your Travel Rewards Visa Signature, the card ending in 6841, today, on this call". Motive: "the $95 annual fee that just showed up on your statement is what finally pushed you" — stated as a reason, not a refund request. Authorisation: "fine confirming or clicking through anything yourself if the agent sends it to you".
- Unknown to the caller: balance and points ("the agent can look those up").
- Conditional, passive responses only: cash for the points into checking "If the agent tells you the points would be lost when the card closes"; autopay from Interest Checking ending 7730 "If the agent says the balance that is left has to be set to pay automatically before the card can be closed", preferring autopay to paying today; "If the agent mentions the annual fee coming off, you say good"; declines retention offers. The simulator never initiates the fee refund, the cash-out or the autopay.
- Identity: 8045550171, 1979-11-02, 7154 → "Identity verified … (3 detail(s) matched this attempt)".

### 5. Tool sequence, owners, dependencies, terminal state

1. `find_customers` → `verify_customer_identity` (agent); `find_card_accounts`, `find_card_transactions`, `find_checking_accounts` (agent).
2. `refund_closing_annual_fee_cfb04f99` (agent; unlock + call) — 95.00 bank_error.
3. `set_closing_card_autopay_dbe1c3a9` (agent unlocks for user; user runs) — fixed_amount 291.82 from 74012327….
4. `cash_out_closing_card_points_6700a44f` (agent unlocks for user; user runs) — 13271 / 132.71 to 74012327….
5. `confirm_card_closure_806ea607` (agent unlocks for user; user runs) — autopay_option fixed_amount.

Dependencies derivable from business principles: 3 → 5 (option kept = option in force at confirmation; a card closed owing money must leave closure with a collecting autopay); 4 → 5 (points still on the card at confirmation are forfeited; the closure is to take effect with no unredeemed points). The value of 3 does not depend on 2 having posted (the ledger figure excludes the fee the closing takes back either way). An order of {2, 3} before 4 is stated only by the workflow doc, which itself says the two sides "touch separate things … and neither alters the other's figures" (see H5). Terminal state as observed in item 4D.

### 6. Problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

Root P0 (asked): close the card by the cardholder's confirmation.

H1 — P0 depends on P1 "cash out all remaining points first" (P1 → P0). **read off.**
- Blocked-side principle (closure_confirmation): "A closure recorded this way forfeits nothing the cardholder could still take: at the moment it takes effect, the card holds no unredeemed points."
- Depended-on rules: rewards_redemption_and_forfeiture: "Because confirmation of a closure extinguishes whatever points are left, a cardholder who is giving up a card keeps the value of its points only by redeeming them while the card is still open." — a single sentence stating the order. Workflow doc (rewards_card_closure_settlement): "The cash-out can deliver their value only while the card remains open, and the confirmation rests on that value having been taken." — states the order outright.
- Records: rewards_balance 13271; active checking 74012327.

H2 — P0 depends on P2 "record a fixed-amount closing autopay for what remains owed" (P2 → P0). **read off.**
- Blocked-side principles: remaining_balance_at_closure: "A card closed while it still owes must come out of the closure carrying an automatic payment able to collect what remains."; autopay_source_at_closure: "The instruction read is the one standing on the card when the confirmation takes effect; an instruction changed during the same consultation is read as changed." With the card's autopay `none` and no source, confirmation now would carry `none` → violates the first principle; therefore P2 first. This part alone would be derived.
- But the workflow doc states it: "The collecting instruction the cardholder has recorded is therefore what the closed card keeps, provided it is in place when the cardholder confirms." and lists "A closing automatic payment, drawn on the cardholder's active PCB checking account, is put in force for the money that remains".

H3 — P2's amount depends on P3 "refund the annual fee still in its refund window" (value dependency P3 → P2). **read off.**
- Derivable from ledger_balance_owed ("a fee that the closing itself takes back off the card lies outside it") + annual_fee_billing_and_refund (30-day window, whole fee, bank error) + record (annual fee 95.00 posted 2026-09-05).
- Stated by the workflow doc: "The sum therefore rests on a ledger from which the refundable annual fee has already gone."

H4 — P3 is itself triggered by P0 (closing within 30 days of posting). **derived** from annual_fee_billing_and_refund + account_closure ("Where the annual fee posted within its refund window, it is taken back as the annual fee terms provide") + record; also listed in the workflow doc ("The agent's part is to reverse the annual fee that is still refundable") → **read off** as well.

H5 — ordering {P3, P2} before P1. **read off, and not derivable from any business principle.** The workflow doc: "The cash-out and the collecting instruction touch separate things … and neither alters the other's figures. This procedure nonetheless treats the whole position on what remains owed, the fee refund together with the instruction that collects the rest, as the settled ground against which the cardholder disposes of the rewards, so that every handling of the case runs the same way." No other visible sentence or record entails this order; a solver reading only the business docs would treat P1 and {P2, P3} as unordered.

Additionally the workflow doc's opening describes exactly this task's combination: "a rewards card that its cardholder wishes to close when the card is still active, still owes money, still has points it has not redeemed, and bears an annual fee whose posting falls inside the window in which that fee is refundable", and its section "The parts and who performs them" enumerates the parts with their owners. The runtime schema of `cash_out_closing_card_points_6700a44f` also says "The cardholder uses this before a card closes so its points are not lost."

Resulting order: P3 (refund) → P2 (closing autopay) → P1 (cash-out) → P0 (confirm), where only P1 → P0 and P2 → P0 are entailed by principles; P3 → P2 is a value dependency satisfied regardless of order; {P3, P2} → P1 is a procedural convention read off the workflow doc.

### Two-way counter-proof

- Support: every figure from quoted KB sentences and tool returns; all four task-tool calls succeeded in the rollout world.
- Closest alternatives excluded:
  - Fixed sum 386.82 (fee included): excluded by ledger_balance_owed ("a fee that the closing itself takes back off the card lies outside it").
  - Fixed sum 343.02 (statement balance) or `statement_balance` kind: excluded by closing_autopay_amount_determination (lower of the two) and closing_balance_autopay_instruction (`fixed_amount` kind).
  - Fixed sum 248.02 (statement balance minus fee): excluded by statement_balance_ceiling ("the new balance shown on the card's most recent statement", recorded 343.02).
  - Closing with autopay `none` and the caller paying later: excluded by remaining_balance_at_closure ("must come out of the closure carrying an automatic payment able to collect what remains").
  - Pro-rated annual fee refund or courtesy ground: excluded ("the whole fee is reversed on the bank error ground"; "`courtesy_waiver`: … never valid for an annual fee").
  - Points at travel worth (0.0125) → 165.89, or to savings / gift card: excluded (cash_out_quantity_determination "The tier's travel worth per point never applies to a deposit"; cash_out_receiving_account).
  - Registering a separate closure request: excluded (closure_confirmation "The agent registers no separate closure request"; account_closure retired-wording paragraph).
- "Do only the one thing asked" (confirm closure now, option none): forfeits 13271 points (rewards_redemption_and_forfeiture, closure_confirmation), leaves a card owing money with no collecting autopay (remaining_balance_at_closure, autopay_source_at_closure → none), and leaves the refundable 95.00 fee on the ledger (annual_fee_billing_and_refund). Excluded by visible principles and records — but each exclusion is also stated outright by the workflow doc, so the hops are read off.

KB-RUNTIME RED items:

**R1-1 — the ledger document rewrites the source's order-bearing value dependency (refund → closing autopay).**
- Symptom: from the visible business documents the blind audit concluded that the closing-autopay figure excludes the refundable annual fee whether or not the refund has already posted; the source makes the figure depend on the refund having posted first.
- Root cause: `card_ext_closing_balance_autopay` defines the fixed amount as the ledger balance "at handling time … minus the sum of … card_fee_reversal … amounts, so any fee already refunded as part of the closing is out of it" — the fee drops out only once its reversal row exists. The KB turns this into an unconditional class: "Because the figure is read from the ledger as it stands when the matter is dealt with, a fee that the closing itself takes back off the card lies outside it."
- Evidence: KB `doc_card_ledger_balance_owed_8e0c0f58`, paragraph after the Definition table (quoted above); source rule sentence quoted above; workflow `order_rationale` step 0→1; GT argument_uniqueness_tracing for `autopay_amount`; blind item 5 sentence, written before reveal.
- Effect: under the KB wording two readings stand — (a) the fee is excluded by definition, so autopay-before-refund also gives 291.82; (b) the ledger is read as posted, so autopay-before-refund gives min(386.82, 343.02) = 343.02 — and only the workflow document's explicit sentence "The sum therefore rests on a ledger from which the refundable annual fee has already gone" brings back the source order. The source reason for workflow step order 0→1 is therefore not entailed by the business documents at the source's strength; it is recoverable only by reading off the workflow document (see the policy_kb file, explicitness E1-3).
- Scored value: not moved for a solver that follows the visible KB (it reaches 291.82 either way); the divergence is in the entailed dependency, not in the terminal state.
- Affected document and location: `doc_card_ledger_balance_owed_8e0c0f58` ("Because the figure is read from the ledger …" sentence); echoed in `doc_card_rewards_card_closure_settlement_49581eab` § "What each part relies on", bullet 1.
